title: ALMA discovery of Punctum, a highly polarized millimeter source in the nuclear starburst galaxy NGC 4945
question: What are the millimeter polarization properties of the compact sources in the central region of the active starburst galaxy NGC 4945, and what is the physical origin of the newly discovered highly polarized source Punctum?

data.sensitivity: S1: 0.017 mJy/beam; S2: 0.014 mJy/beam; archival 2018.1.01236.S: 0.014 mJy/beam; archival Band 7: 3sigma = 0.3 mJy/beam; archival Band 8: 1sigma = 3.5 mJy

what.value: ATCA (17, 19, 21, 23 GHz) and LBA (2.3 GHz) detection limits for NGC 4945

evidence.quote: According to ATCA data from (cite: lenc2009), no specific or isolated source corresponding to *Punctum* was detected at frequencies of 17, 19, 21, and 23 GHz, with 1$\sigma$ detection limits of 0.25–0.34 mJy/beam at a resolution of $\sim$0.5$''$.

what.value: Distance to NGC 4945 of D = 3.72 Mpc measured via tip of the red giant branch

evidence.quote: Our sample, drawn from the list of compact mm-bright RQ AGNs compiled by (cite: ricci23), included NGC 4945, a well-known nearby galaxy at a redshift of $z = 0.0023$ and a distance of $D = 3.72$ Mpc[^1].
[^1]: The redshift-independent distance was measured using the tip of the red giant branch (see (cite: koss22)) and is consistent with the measurements from (cite: karachentsev07).

what.value: Blazar number counts used to extrapolate the probability of a background blazar within 3.4'' of the nucleus

evidence.quote: Moreover, while the number density of blazars at such low flux levels is not commonly reported, we extrapolated the number counts from (cite: tucci11) and estimated that the probability of finding a blazar with a flux of $\sim$0.1 mJy within 3.4$''$ of the nucleus of NGC 4945 is less than 0.4%.

what.value: Star-formation rate of ~2-8 M_sun yr^-1 for NGC 4945

evidence.quote: Given the calculated star-formation rate of $\sim$2–8 $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$ for NGC 4945 (cite: roy10), we can estimate the supernova rate using the relation from (cite: Cappellaro99), yielding $\sim$2–8 SN per 100 years.

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA Band 3 Stokes I, Q, U data and spectral cubes
recipe.method: Process Band 3 observations for epochs S1 and S2 using CASA and the ALMA Pipeline, generate clean images using tclean with Briggs weighting, and reprocess data into spectral cubes with 31.2 MHz channel width.
key_parameters: channel width = 31.2 MHz for spectral cubes

recipe.goal: Create polarized intensity and debiased polarization degree maps and identify persistent polarized sources
recipe.method: Calculate polarized intensity P = sqrt(Q^2 + U^2) and polarization degree PD = P/I, debias PD following Montier et al. (2015a,b), mask regions with S/N < 5, and compare S1 and S2 maps to confirm persistent polarized sources.

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux, spectral index, line emission, and archival ALMA fluxes for Punctum
recipe.method: Measure continuum flux averaged over all spectral windows and in each of the 4 spectral windows for S1 and S2, fit a power law to obtain the spectral index alpha, extract 31.2 MHz binned spectra to check for molecular lines, and measure flux/spectral index in archival high-resolution ALMA data.
assumptions: Flux uncertainties are the quadrature sum of 5% calibration uncertainty and image background rms

recipe.goal: Estimate multi-wavelength luminosity upper limits and physical properties of Punctum
recipe.method: Extract archival Chandra X-ray spectrum and fit phabs*powerlaw and cflux in XSPEC for the 3.0-6.0 keV upper limit; derive 23 GHz luminosity upper limit from ATCA non-detection; compute isotropic mm luminosity and estimate synchrotron self-absorption size using Eq. 19 of Laor & Behar (2008).
assumptions: Punctum is located in NGC 4945 at D = 3.72 Mpc
Standard cosmological parameters (H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7)

answer_key.quantity: Punctum weighted mean spectral index alpha

evidence.quote: Indeed, the *Punctum*’s spectral index of $-1.5$ $\pm$ 1.7, calculated as the weighted mean from two epochs, aligns with typical pulsar spectral indices, with a mean value of $\alpha = -1.8$ (cite: maron00).

answer_key.quantity: Punctum polarization degree (epoch S1)

evidence.quote: In the PD map, the source exhibits an exceptionally high level of polarization, consistent across both epochs: 51% $\pm$ 14% for S1 and 50% $\pm$ 14% for S2, with the polarization angle of 133.2$^\circ$ $\pm$ 7.9$^\circ$ for S1 and 130.6$^\circ$ $\pm$ 7.8$^\circ$ for S2.
